title: Day 782: Thousands March in Culiacán for Peace on Second Anniversary of Chapitos–Mayos War
detail: Thousands of Culiacán residents marched on Sunday, September 13, 2026, to demand security and peace, two years after the Chapitos–Mayos war began on September 9, 2024. The mobilization started with a 7:00 AM mass followed by a march from La Lomita, and included search collectives for missing persons and families of victims carrying signs reading 'We don't want fear, we want peace' and 'When a mother cries, we all cry.' Organizers said the conflict has left more than 3,000 people killed and thousands more disappeared or displaced. The march came a day after ten homicides were recorded across Sinaloa state — four in Culiacán, five in Mazatlán and one in Escuinapa — underscoring that violence had not abated ahead of the demonstration. Local business chambers said more than 5,000 businesses have closed since the war began, and marchers recalled a one-year-old child killed by stray gunfire the previous week. The Bishop of Culiacán told the crowd, 'Deténganse, miren lo que está sucediendo... Ningún poder, dinero, territorio o ambición vale más que una vida humana' ('Stop, look at what is happening... No power, money, territory or ambition is worth more than a human life').

media.caption: Thousands march in Culiacán demanding peace and security, two years into the Chapitos–Mayos war, September 13, 2026

title: Day 782: Man and Woman Found Shot Dead Near Pueblo Nuevo Sports Center in Escuinapa
detail: At around 9:03 AM on Sunday, September 13, 2026, the bodies of a man and a woman were found alongside a red bicycle beneath a tree on a road near the Polideportivo in Escuinapa's Pueblo Nuevo neighborhood, in Sinaloa's southern gateway municipality. Both were later identified as María Oralia 'N', 47, and José Feliciano 'N', 38. Both bore gunshot wounds; the woman's face was reportedly covered. Investigators recovered multiple spent cartridges at the scene. Forensic personnel and National Guard agents processed the site before the bodies were transferred to the Medical Examiner's office in Mazatlán. The case brought Escuinapa's 2026 femicide count to 15, and came a day after the municipality recorded a separate homicide alongside Highway Mexico 15.

media.caption: Coverage of the double homicide near the Polideportivo in Escuinapa's Pueblo Nuevo neighborhood, September 13, 2026
